problem.text: GLANCE reports that increasing routing budget K can improve heterophilous-node accuracy but that routing too many nodes can harm accuracy, and that a single homophily threshold is ineffective across datasets.

source_spans.quote: We find that increasing $K$ tends to lead to steady gains on heterophilous nodes, while leaving performance on the homophilous nodes mostly unchanged.

Importantly, we also observe that routing too many nodes can harm accuracy (as seen in Table 10 for full-batch routing), as easy nodes well modeled by the GNN can become misclassified when the LLM is unnecessarily used.
Thus, a single homophily threshold that only routes heterophilous nodes would be ineffective for maximizing performance, and additional context is needed.

problem.text: SUMMQ reports BERTScore-F1 peaking at three refinement iterations and then declining, while ROUGE-1 does not rise monotonically across iterations 3 to 5 on the same axis.

source_spans.quote: Performance generally improves from 1 to 3 iterations, with BERTScore-F1 peaking at 62.76, but further iterations yield diminishing or negative returns.

problem.text: HILA reports agent scaling has diminishing and less stable gains while cost rises sharply, and collaborative rounds are non-monotonic with accuracy peaking at an intermediate depth while token usage continues to rise.

mechanism.text: Added resource raises a task metric only while marginal task-relevant evidence or coordination benefit exceeds marginal redundancy/weak relevance, over-routing of already-easy cases, and cost/token/coordination overhead.

Metrics differ in how sharply they penalize these overheads, so noise-sensitive metrics should peak earlier than coverage/task-success metrics, and cost-inclusive metrics should peak earlier than pure quality metrics.
The turning point is therefore predicted to be a metric- and task-conditioned crossing, not a fixed resource number.
Whether a common determinant exists across the five resource axes rather than axis-specific mechanisms is unknown.
